result.title: Adaptive Decoding Methods for Token-Efficient Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Rollout decoding affects both which trajectories are used for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and how many completion tokens are spent collecting them. We study whether candidate-token support should remain fixed or widen during training in the context of rollout sampling efficiency. Our main schedule moves from top-K=10 to K=20 and then to full support as the attempted-token budget increases. In a 4B code-RLVR setting, the schedule has a higher interpolated 150M-token validation value than its matched fixed-K=10 continuation in all three runs, with a mean gain of $1.80{\pm}0.42$ points. The schedule also performs comparably to a separately trained fixed-K=20 baseline, the strongest fixed-support setting in our sweep. Follow-up experiments suggest that late widening to full support is the most promising variant, although the evidence remains noisy, and mixed-reward-group diagnostics do not clearly explain the gain. An exploratory single-run test replay yields identical point estimates for the schedule and fixed $K=10$. Overall, our results show that rollout support is an important control for sampling efficiency in RLVR and motivate further study of adaptive support schedules.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 RLVR 中 rollout 解码的候选 token 支持集应固定还是随训练扩大，提出由 top-K=10 到 K=20 再到全支持的调度，并在 4B 代码 RLVR 上用等 token 预算的验证值与固定 K 基线比较采样效率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「随预算渐进扩大候选支持」的调度思路，可供核查是否能迁移为 LVR 中潜推理步数、候选宽度或思考预算的动态调度与停止策略；但该文仅在纯文本 RLVR 上验证，未涉及视觉或多模态状态。
